item.title: Journalisme de guerre et intelligence artificielle : Entre usages et défis
item.description: This article analyzes the use of artificial intelligence (AI) in war journalism, exploring its innovations, challenges, and impacts. It is based on a survey of 38 freelance journalists working in conflict zones. The study reveals that AI strengthens existing practices such as automation and combating disinformation while also raising ethical and technical concerns. Despite these advancements, the role of the human journalist remains central to ensuring ethical and high-quality reporting.

item.title: Motivations of Public Relations Professionals to Use Artificial Intelligence: A Study on Türkiye
item.description: As all the other sectors, PR sector, which is evolving from traditional to digital, must also integrate AI into its process of change and development. item.title: L’usage de l’Intelligence Artificielle en journalisme: Pourquoi la Tunisie connaît un retard dans son adoption ?
item.description: The objective of this research is to study how Tunisian journalists think about the use of AI in their profession. This work is based on a qualitative study conducted in 2024 through 21 interviews with journalistic professionals in Tunisia. The results highlight the clear evidence that the integration of AI into Tunisian journalism is inevitable. item.description: Social media profoundly influences modern society, offering both opportunities and risks for communication. item.title: Publication Trends in Artificial Intelligence and Journalism
item.description: This study examines the publication trends, dominant research topics, and regional disparities in academic knowledge production on artificial intelligence (AI) in journalism. item.title: Personal Branding in the Classical Music Industry in the Age of Social Media
item.description: This article explores personal branding in classical music through the lens of digital media, focusing on self-representation, communication, and visibility.
